newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S.Africa says diplomatic move to help HK consulate.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says diplomatic move to help HK consulate.

text.p: South Africa's move to switch recognition to Beijing from Taipei will help Pretoria maintain a Hong Kong consulate after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule, South Africa's Hong Kong Consul-General said on Thursday.

The move to switch diplomatic ties "has made the negotiations far more easy to enter into, because it's important for us to remain in Hong Kong", Delina De Villers-Steenkamp told Hong Kong government radio.
"Had we not recognised Beijing it would have been more difficult for South Africa to remain here in present form," she said.

Hong Kong will revert to Beijing's control at midnight June 30, 1997, ending over 150 years of colonial rule. Countries with diplomatic office here must negotiate with China on their status after the handover.
South African President Nelson Mandela announced on Wednesday that Petoria would switch diplomatic recognition from Taipei to Beijing by the end of 1997.
China and Taiwan have been diplomatic rivals since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
Beijing regards Taiwan as a rebel province and has sought to push the island into diplomatic isolation. Taiwan insists that its 21 million people should have a voice in international affairs.
